decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 2 percent.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to lower its target for the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 2 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed lowered the benchmark interest rate by a smaller increment than its previous 75 basis point cut, bringing the rate down to 2 percent.

changes.quote: Recent information indicates that economic activity remains weak.
changes.explanation: This simplifies the description of the economy from previous statements, acknowledging ongoing weakness.

changes.quote: Household and business spending has been subdued and labor markets have softened further.
changes.explanation: Consumer and business spending remains weak while job market conditions have deteriorated more.

changes.quote: Although readings on core inflation have improved somewhat, energy and other commodity prices have increased, and some indicators of inflation expectations have risen in recent months.
changes.explanation: The Fed noted that while core inflation improved, rising energy and commodity prices and climbing inflation expectations remain a concern.

changes.quote: Voting against were Richard W. Fisher and Charles I. Plosser, who preferred no change in the target for the federal funds rate at this meeting.
changes.explanation: Two members dissented because they wanted to keep the interest rate unchanged instead of cutting it.

tone_quotes.quote: Recent information indicates that economic activity remains weak.
Household and business spending has been subdued and labor markets have softened further.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 12.75% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 3.77% and moved -8 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.88% would fall by about $15.31 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 5.1%, and employers added an average of -45k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 4% over the past year (March 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.2%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -1.7% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -6 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.02% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Committee will continue to monitor economic and financial developments to decide future actions. Educational forecast models suggest a 66% chance of a hold and a 34% chance of a cut at the next meeting.
